Design changes from v2

1 · Dual-language stats row

Every quant stat now has a plain-English translation as the primary text, with the quant notation as smaller technical caption below or right.

β = 1.42 → "Reacts 1.4× more than S&P 500"

E[R] = +0.74R → "Expected profit · 74¢ per $1 risked"

Wilson LB = 0.52, n=47 → "Honest win-rate floor · 52% (95% confident)"

2 · Enhanced plan ladder

Top labels now read as "Sell-if-wrong $240 · −$1,375" — action verb + price + dollar impact on $25K position.

Bottom labels show R-multiple + hit-probability + typical days-to-target:
+2.9R · 42% hit · typ. 8 days

Risk-reward summary in the foot: "Lose $1 to win $2.93 (T1) or $4.89 (T2)"

Background zones color-code R-multiple bands (loss / +1R / +2-3R / +3-5R)

Monte Carlo path overlay — 6 sample simulated paths showing the spread

3 · Probability + EV in dollars

Strip still shows the stacked probability bar, but now labeled "Likely outcome in 5 days" not "P(close at 5d)".

EV translates to dollars: "Expected profit +$1,839 per trade" beside the quant E[R] = +0.74R.

Each probability segment shows its category name (STOP / FLAT / T1 / T2 / EXT) below the percentage.

4 · Lens votes as stance words

Replaces raw z-scores with stance words: Expensive, Strong, Neutral, Choppy, Buying, Acceptable, Positive, Suitable.

Z-score + significance markers shown below in mono as the auditable backing.

Conflict callout uses natural language: "Value vs Swing+Insider+News"

5 · Verdict block · context-aware

Verdict pill now sits with a conviction tag ("HIGH CONVICTION · TIER 1") and a sentence-form thesis:

"The system rates this 78 out of 100. Setup is an impulse-catalyst play — enter on momentum, hold through the catalyst window, take profit at +55% / +92%."

6 · Audit footer · compact technical

The footer remains in mono · keeps quant-grade audit data: λ_kelly, HMM, drift, PF, gates, timestamp.

Not designed for the common reader — it's the receipt for the quant who wants to verify.

UX principle applied · "primary plain, secondary technical"
Every screen element teaches the common user without dumbing down for the quant. Plain-English labels carry the verb (sell, buy, profit, risk) and the dollar amount they care about; quant notation hangs as a smaller caption underneath or to the right. A novice scans the bold English and acts. A quant scans the mono captions and verifies. Same screen, two audiences, no compromise.
